newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Five firms to bid in Ecuador telephone sale.
newsitem.headline: Five firms to bid in Ecuador telephone sale.

text.p: Five international firms from the United States, Europe and Asia will bid in the upcoming privatization of 35 percent of Ecuador's telephone company Emetel, a government official said Friday.

The president of the National Modernization Council, Omar Quintana, said the government had received all necessary documentation to participate in the sale from MCI Communications Corp, GTE Corp, Italy's Stet SpA, Spain's Telefonica de Espana SA, and South Korea's Korea Telecom.
"We didn't get ten firms but we have five. That is more than the number of companies which showed up for telephone privatizations in Colombia, Argentina, Mexico, Peru and Chile," Quintana said.
Ecuador hopes to raise $1.0 billion from the sale of 35 percent of Emetel, which it plans to carry out next April, an official source said.
Ecuador has some 800,000 telephone lines for its 11.7 million people, one of the lowest rates in Latin America, and expects to raise that figure to 2.5 million by 2000, Quintana said.
